questions.answer: I'm from Sirajganj, a modest town in the north of Bangladesh, right beside the Jamuna river. It's about four hours from Dhaka by road, and I've lived there most of my life, so it has a certain [[tranquillity]] that feels like home.

questions.q: What do you like most about your hometown?
questions.answer: Without doubt, the river. In the evenings I often walk along the Jamuna embankment, and watching the sun set over the water is incredibly [[soothing]]. The people are warm and welcoming too, which gives it a real sense of community.

questions.q: Is your hometown a good place for visitors?
questions.answer: It's not a major tourist destination, but it has its charms. Sirajganj is known for its handloom weaving, and visitors can take a boat trip on the Jamuna. It suits anyone who enjoys a slower, more [[laid-back]] pace.

questions.q: Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
questions.answer: Quite a lot, actually. There are more shops, better roads and far more traffic than when I was younger. Some of it is welcome progress, but part of me misses how quiet and [[unspoilt]] it used to feel.

questions.q: Do you prefer living in a city or the countryside?
questions.answer: That's a tough one. I enjoy the energy of a city, but I genuinely appreciate the calm of the countryside. Honestly, the [[ideal]] for me would be a quieter town that isn't too far from a city.
